section_summary: This section consists chiefly of mass-petition sheets opposing the export of scrap iron and other war materials to Japan, with signatures collected in San Diego County, the Imperial Valley, Yuma and other Southern California and Arizona communities. It also contains a State Department reply explaining why the Neutrality Act did not authorize an embargo on scrap iron, together with two transmittal letters from peace activists forwarding additional batches of signatures. A final fragment records circulation or filing of the material.

subfiles.title: Petition against shipment of scrap iron and war material to Japan, San Diego-area signatures
subfiles.from: Petition signers collected through the Peace Committee, San Diego
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: San Diego-area residents protest the shipment of scrap iron and other war material to Japan.
subfiles.summary: These pages continue a petition begun before page 65 and contain handwritten names and addresses from San Diego, National City, La Mesa, Santee, La Jolla and nearby communities. The printed heading addresses President Roosevelt and Secretary Hull and asks that shipments of scrap iron and other war materials to Japan be stopped. Each sheet directs completed petitions to the Peace Committee at 3546 First Avenue, San Diego.

subfiles.title: State Department reply concerning the petition and the Neutrality Act
subfiles.from: Charles W. Yost, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: W. J. Sherman, San Diego, California
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges 983 petition signatures and explains why existing law does not authorize a ban on scrap-iron exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Yost thanks Sherman and Kate Beming for 983 signatures, enclosing the 1937 Neutrality Act and pamphlet; scrap iron isn't a covered arm and no statute allows prohibiting it; arms licenses since July 1, 1937 were $14,267,823.21 for China and $10,793,865.38 for Japan.

subfiles.title: San Diego transmittal letter enclosing additional petition signatures
subfiles.about: A San Diego correspondent forwards nearly 800 more signatures protesting scrap-iron exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: San Diego writer encloses nearly 800 more signatures, for a total OCR renders as over 9,500, invoking the Rome-Berlin Axis; signature illegible.

subfiles.title: Petition against shipment of scrap iron and war material to Japan, additional California and Arizona signatures
subfiles.from: Petition signers collected through the Peace Committee, San Diego
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: Residents of San Diego County, Yuma, Pasadena and other communities add their names to the anti-export petition.
subfiles.summary: The printed petition repeats the demand that scrap iron and other war material no longer be shipped to Japan. The sheets contain handwritten signatures and addresses from San Diego and its suburbs, Yuma and the Imperial Valley, and communities including Pasadena, Altadena, Los Angeles, Santa Barbara and Long Beach. The wide geographic distribution shows the Peace Committee extending its signature campaign well beyond central San Diego.

subfiles.title: Women's International League transmittal of more than one thousand signatures
subfiles.from: Kate H. Beming, for the San Diego Peace Committee and Women's International League for Peace and Freedom
subfiles.to: Cordell Hull, State Department, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.about: The San Diego peace organizations forward another thousand signatures opposing American material support for Japan's war in China.
subfiles.summary: Women's International League sender encloses over a thousand signatures against arming Japan, raising the San Diego total to six thousand with another thousand coming, and thanks Hull for trade agreements.

subfiles.title: Petition against shipment of scrap iron and war material to Japan, National City–Yuma–Imperial Valley signatures
subfiles.from: Petition signers collected through the Peace Committee, San Diego
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Cordell Hull
subfiles.about: A further group of petition sheets records signatures chiefly from National City, Yuma, Somerton and Imperial Valley communities.
subfiles.summary: These sheets continue the same printed appeal against shipments of scrap iron and other war materials to Japan. Large clusters of signers come from National City, Yuma and Somerton, with additional names from El Centro, Winterhaven, Calexico, Imperial, Westmorland, Brawley, Coronado and San Diego. The sheets again direct completed petitions to the Peace Committee at 3546 First Avenue in San Diego.
